newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Delayed Zambian polls set for November 18.
newsitem.headline: Delayed Zambian polls set for November 18.

text.p: Zambian President Frederick Chiluba on Saturday set November 18 as the date for presidential and parliamentary elections which were due to have been held by the end of October.

"I am happy to announce the presidential and parliamentary elections will be held on November 18," Chiluba told a rally of his Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) party in the central town of Kabwe.
He said he had dissolved parliament effective from October 18.

Parliament's five-year term was due to expire on October 31 and critics of Chiluba have been saying that his failure to name a date for new elections this month would leave a constitutional power vacuum.

Chiluba's government has said new laws it passed recently allowed it to remain in office up to three months beyond the dissolution of parliament, giving it a breathing space until the end of January to hold elections.
But Dean Mungomba, leader of the opposition Zambia Democratic Congress, speaking before Chiluba's remarks on Saturday, said:
"On October 31, Mr Chiluba's term of office comes to an end. No amount of legal gymnastics can change that fact.
"We shall have no recognition of this government after October 31, and therefore reserve the right to take whatever steps to ensure he does not extend his stay in office beyond October 31."
Chiluba's government has already angered its opponents by amending the constitution to prevent anyone who has served two terms as president from running again.
This rules out Kenneth Kaunda, head of the opposition United National Independence Party (UNIP) who led Zambia to independence from Britain in 1964.
